title: Inflammatory neuropathy in mouse and primate models of colorectal cancer
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76683-1

Whether cancer damages peripheral nerves before treatment is unclear. Here, authors show that colorectal tumors drive inflammation and disrupt neuronal lipids, causing subtle sensory pathology in mice and monkeys that may persist in survivors.

title: Observed poleward heat transport by mesoscale eddies in the deep Southern Ocean
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76674-2

Two decades of Argo observations reveal that mesoscale eddies redistribute heat in the deep Southern Ocean at rates comparable in magnitude to surface eddy heat transport, with about 60% of this deep transport originating from the Indian Ocean sector.

title: Amiloride mitigates respiratory distress caused by WFDC2 deficiency via inhibiting the epithelial sodium channel
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76582-5

This study identifies a WFDC2 mutation that causes a severe cystic-fibrosis-like airway disease in humans and mice. The mutation overactivates the epithelial sodium channel, and treatment with the drug amiloride improves survival and lung function in affected mice.

title: Zinc displacement and metabolic interference: cobalt ion-mediated therapy for broad-spectrum CRKP-resistant pneumonia via inhalable microspheres
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76666-2

The global rise of carbapenem-resistant bacteria, driven by enzymes such as KPC-2 and OXA-48 as well as metallo-β-lactamases, poses a major challenge to antibiotic therapy. Here, the authors develop a cobalt-based microsphere platform for the delivery of meropenem, leveraging Co²⁺ as a metal-based resistance breaker to overcome multiple resistance mechanisms. In a mouse model of drug-resistant pneumonia, the treatment improved survival, reduced bacterial burden, and mitigated excessive inflammation, highlighting a promising strategy for combating multidrug-resistant infections.

title: Origin of circular and triangular pores in electron-irradiated hexagonal boron nitride
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76612-2

For two decades, triangular nanopores have been known to form in 2D boron nitride during electron microscopy. Researchers reveal this to be due to oxygen in the microscope column, allowing pore shaping via atmospheric control.

title: Moiré-induced modulation of out-of-plane elasticity in twisted hBN
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76466-8

Twisted hBN moiré patterns are shown to modulate the effective out-of-plane elastic response, enabling AFM visualization through a stacking-dependent elastic landscape.

title: Overcoming the conversion-selectivity trade-off in plasma catalytic conversion of methane to ethylene
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76709-8

Non-thermal plasma (NTP) offers a low-temperature route for methane activation but is hindered by high energy consumption and limited ethylene selectivity. Here, the authors develop a pure-silica self-pillared pentasil zeolite that improves methane-to-ethylene conversion under NTP conditions.

title: A flexible repertoire of wound closure strategies precedes whole-body regeneration
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76555-8

Animals capable of whole-body regeneration can heal virtually any wound. Here they show that Hofstenia miamia accomplishes this feat through variable morphogenetic strategies that depend on which epithelial layers are damaged, revealing a versatile toolkit for repair.
